questions.question: Who among the following wrote ‘Nirmala’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Munshi Premchand**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **'Nirmala'** is a famous novel written by **Munshi Premchand**, one of the most celebrated authors in Hindi literature.
 
• The novel was published in **1925** and addresses critical issues like dowry and the plight of women in Indian society.
 
• Premchand's writing style in 'Nirmala' is characterized by its realism, focusing on the socio-economic struggles of the time.
 
• Munshi Premchand is widely regarded as the **'Upanyas Samrat'**
 
• He has written numerous other masterpieces, including **'Godaan'**, **'Karmabhoomi'**, and **'Sevasadan'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dowry System:** The dowry system, which plays a central role in 'Nirmala,' refers to the practice of transferring parental property or wealth to a daughter at her marriage. It has been a critical social issue in India.
 
• **Realism in Literature:** Premchand's works are known for their realism, portraying the struggles of the common man and highlighting social injustices and economic disparities.
 
• **Hindi Literature Evolution:** Munshi Premchand significantly contributed to the evolution of Hindi literature by transitioning it from romanticism to addressing real-life social and economic issues.
 
• **Munshi Premchand's Legacy:** He is celebrated not only in Hindi literature but also in Urdu literature, where he began his writing career before switching to Hindi.
 
• **Impact of 'Nirmala':** The novel continues to be a subject of academic and literary discussion due to its progressive portrayal of women's issues and its critique of societal norms.

questions.question: Who was the author of the three-act play, 'Post Office'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Rabindranath Tagore.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rabindranath Tagore** was the author of the three-act play, 'Post Office' of **1912**.
 
• It concerns Amal, a child confined to his adoptive uncle's home by an incurable disease. 
 
• W. Andrew Robinson and Krishna Dutta note that the play "continues to occupy a special place in Tagore's reputation, both within Bengal and in the wider world." It was written in four days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rabindranath Tagore:**

 
 
• He was the recipient of the **Nobel Prize for Literature in 1913 **and is internationally known as a great poet. He was born in the** year 1861**, in **Calcutta, Bengal**.
 
• From his earliest days, Rabindranath grew up in a house where all the changes emerging in Indian society of that time were being felt in his day-to-day life. Tagore's Philosophy of Education: Tagore, laid great stress and emphasis on the aesthetic development of the senses in his philosophy of education.
 
• He argued that the development of the senses was as important as intellectual development. He, therefore, gave prominence to music, literature, art, dance, and drama in the daily life of the school.
 
• Tagore believed in the all-around development of personality and in his institution education continues to address the all-around development of the students.
 
• Tagore's theory of education is marked by naturalistic & aesthetic values. He had a belief that **"The widest road leading to the solution of all our problems is education."**
 
• Education can develop a new pattern of life that culminates in the realization of a universal man. Tagore's system of education emphasizes the intellectual, physical, social, moral economic, and spiritual aspects of human life by which a man can develop an integrated personality.
 
• Tagore believed that along with education, economic upliftment is also necessary.

questions.question: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘The Room on the Roof’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ruskin Bond**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Room on the Roof**

 
 
• **Ruskin Bond **wrote the book 'The Room on the Roof'.
 
• It was Bond's **first writing** venture.
 
• When Bond finished the book at the age of **17**, it was awarded the **1957 John Llewellyn Rhys Prize**.
 
• It tells the story of an** orphaned Anglo-Indian boy who flees his oppressive guardian to live with his Indian friends**.
 
• Bond's experiences of living in a rented terrace flat in Dehradun **served as the basis for the book**.
 
• **Partha Pratim Das** has translated 'The Room on the Roof' into the first** authorised Bengali edition**, which will be released by Book Farm in 2022 under the title **"Chilekothar Ghar."​**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ruskin Bond**

 
 
• **Author Ruskin Bond is an Anglo Indian** and was born on** May 19, 1934**.
 
• More than **500 short stories, articles, and novels, including 64 books for children**, have been written by Bond.
 
• The **Sahitya Akademi Award** was given to him in** 1992 for" Our Trees Still Grow in Dehra." **
 
• In **1999 and 2014**, he received the** Padma Shri and Padma Bhushan**, respectively. 
 
• **'A Flight of Pigeons'**, a Bond novel, served as the inspiration for the **1978 Bollywood film Junoon**.
 
• It was directed by** Shyam Benegal** and produced by **Shashi Kapoor**.

questions.question: Who among the following is the author of the book ‘The Complete Adventures of Feluda’?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satyajit Ray**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Satyajit Ray, an iconic Indian filmmaker and write**r, created the character Feluda, a detective whose stories are set in India

 
 
• and are beloved by readers for their wit, intelligence, and engaging mystery plots.
 
 
 
• He is **often compared to Sherlock Holmes**, with his keen observational skills and analytical mind.
 
• **Feluda** is a fictional Bengali detective introduced by Satyajit Ray in 1965.
 
• He first appeared in the story **“Feludar Goyendagiri”** published in the children’s magazine **Sandesh**, which Ray edited.
 
• The stories are usually narrated by Feluda's cousin, **Topshe**, who plays the role of Watson-like companion.
 
• **The Complete Adventures of Feluda"** is a collection that brings together all of Feluda’s stories, spanning multiple volumes.
 
• The stories cover a wide range of mysteries, from murders to thefts and missing persons, often set against the backdrop of Indian cities, towns, and historical locations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mrinal Sen**

 
 
• He is one of the pioneers of Indian parallel cinema, known for making films that address social issues, political struggles, and the lives of the marginalized.
 
• His films, such as **"Bhuvan Shome" (1969)** and **"Mrigayaa" (1976)**,
 
 
• reflect the harsh realities of Indian society and deal with topics like class conflict and urbanization.
 
 
 
 
 
• **Ritwik Ghatak**
 
 
• Ritwik Ghatak’s films are marked by their intense emotional depth and cultural context.
 
• His work often drew from his own experience of the **Partition of Bengal**, which profoundly impacted him.
 
• Films like **"Meghe Dhaka Tara" (1960)** and **"Subarnarekha" (1965)** depict the trauma and displacement faced by refugees and marginalized communities.
 
 
 
• **Goutam Ghose**
 
 
• He is known for his work both as a documentarian and a feature filmmaker.
 
• His films often straddle the line between fiction and reality, reflecting deep empathy for rural life and the common people.
 
• Films like **"Padma Nadir Majhi" (1993)** and **"Moner Manush" (2010)** depict the struggles and resilience of ordinary individuals in the face of hardship.

questions.question: Kathasaritsagara, a literary work, was originally composed in which of the following languages?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sanskrit**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathasaritsagara** is a famous literary work originally composed in **Sanskrit**.
 
• It is a renowned collection of Indian legends, fairy tales, and folk tales.
 
• The work is attributed to the author **Somadeva**, who compiled it in the 11th century.
 
• The title "Kathasaritsagara" translates to "Ocean of the Streams of Stories."
 
• This extensive work is an important source for understanding ancient Indian culture and literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
